title: Reverse an Array
description: Given an array, return a new array with the elements in reverse order. Do not mutate the original array.
whatShouldHappen: Create an empty result array.
Loop from the last index down to 0.
Push each element into the result array.
Return the result array.
patternExplanation: Start the loop counter at the last index and decrement it each step — the simplest way to walk a collection from right to left.

title: Check Palindrome
description: Given a string, return true if it reads the same forwards and backwards, false otherwise.
whatShouldHappen: Loop from the last character down to the midpoint.
Compare each character with its mirror from the start.
Return false immediately if any pair does not match.
Return true after the loop completes without a mismatch.
patternExplanation: Compare index i from the start with index (length - 1 - i) from the end, looping only to the midpoint — this is the in-place palindrome check.

title: Reverse a String
description: Given a string, return a new string with the characters in reverse order. Do not use the built-in .reverse() or .split().reverse().join() chain.
whatShouldHappen: Start with an empty result string.
Loop from the last character index down to 0.
Concatenate each character onto the result string.
Return the result.
patternExplanation: Walking the string backwards and concatenating each character builds the reversed string in a single pass — same pattern as reversing an array.

title: Count Down to Zero
description: Given a positive integer n, return an array containing [n, n-1, n-2, ..., 1, 0].
whatShouldHappen: Create an empty result array.
Loop starting from n, while i >= 0, decrementing each step.
Push i into the result array on each iteration.
Return the result array.
patternExplanation: Setting the start value to n and using i-- with a condition i >= 0 is the classic countdown loop — the loop variable itself becomes the data.

title: Find Last Occurrence
description: Given an array and a target value, return the index of the last occurrence of the target. Return -1 if it is not found. Do not use the built-in .lastIndexOf().
whatShouldHappen: Loop from the last index down to 0.
On the first match (which is the last occurrence since we go right-to-left), return the index.
If the loop completes without a match, return -1.
patternExplanation: Iterating from the right means the first match you find is the last occurrence — no need to scan the whole array or track candidates.

title: Find Last Index of Element
description: Given an array and a target value, find the last index where target appears by searching backwards from the end of the array. Return -1 if not found.
whatShouldHappen: Loop from arr.length - 1 down to 0.
If arr[i] === target, return index i immediately.
If loop finishes without finding target, return -1.
patternExplanation: Searching from the end allows finding the last occurrence on the very first match in best-case O(1) time.

title: Reverse Words in a String
description: Given a string s of words separated by spaces, return a string of the words in reverse order concatenated by a single space.
whatShouldHappen: Split s by whitespace filtering out empty strings.
Build a new array by looping through the words from last index down to 0.
Join the reversed words with a single space and return the string.
patternExplanation: Traversing tokenized word arrays backwards reverses token order without mutating individual word character order.

title: Countdown Sequence Generator
description: Given a start positive integer n, return an array with numbers counting down from n to 1.
whatShouldHappen: Initialize seq = [].
Loop from i = n down to 1.
Push i to seq.
Return seq.
patternExplanation: A classic decrementing loop (i--) generates descending numeric ranges cleanly.
